# Final website design brief

# **Final website design brief \- NeoCore for Enterprise**

## *Single source of truth for website design and development*

# **1\. Page mandate**

### **Objective**

Build a focused enterprise landing page that converts qualified buyers into conversations with NeoSapien’s enterprise team. The page must make one proposition immediately clear: NeoCore turns frontline sales conversations into centralized intelligence for pitch adherence, coaching and Voice of Customer.

### **Primary audience, in order**

1\. Sales Excellence, Revenue Transformation and GTM Excellence leaders  
2\. CROs, national or regional sales heads and business-unit leaders  
3\. Sales coaching, L\&D and Customer Insights teams  
4\. IT, data, security and procurement stakeholders validating deployment

### **Primary conversion**

Talk to our enterprise team

### **Secondary actions**

• See a sample analysis \- scrolls to the ungated synthetic example in Fold 4\.  
• See a tailored demo \- opens the same qualification form and is visually subordinate to the primary CTA.

### **Page-wide design rules**

• NeoCore’s intelligence, dashboards and management outputs must receive at least 80% of the page’s visual prominence.  
• Neo One is the low-friction capture input, not the central product story. Keep it to 15–20% or less of any solution visual.  
• Use real product UI wherever available. Label representative screens “Illustrative view.”  
• Avoid stock sales-team photography, device-led hero imagery and equal-sized feature-icon flows.  
• Keep the page to seven folds. Every fold must advance the story or conversion.  
• Use the current NeoSapien enterprise visual system: black or deep-green background, bright green accent, high-contrast white typography and restrained motion.  
• The primary CTA label is always “Talk to our enterprise team.”

### **Navigation**

NeoCore | How it works | Outcomes | Security | FAQ | Talk to our enterprise team  
Use sticky navigation on desktop and a compact mobile header with the primary CTA accessible.

# **2\. Fold-by-fold build specification**

## **Fold 1 \- Hero**

### **Objective**

Communicate the enterprise outcome immediately, without asking the visitor to decode Neo One versus NeoCore.

### **Final copy**

Eyebrow: NeoCore for Enterprise  
Headline: Make frontline sales conversations visible, measurable and actionable.  
Description: Measure pitch adherence, identify coaching priorities and hear the Voice of Customer \- across teams, regions and languages.  
Primary CTA: Talk to our enterprise team  
Secondary text link: See a sample analysis  
Proof line: 140+ languages • Under 2-minute processing • ISO 27001 certified

### **Representation**

Use a 45/55 desktop split: copy on the left, NeoCore management intelligence on the right. Show one coherent dashboard view containing pitch-adherence performance, team or region comparisons, coaching priorities and emerging Voice of Customer themes. A small Neo One device or capture signal may feed into the dashboard from one edge; it must not become the hero object. Do not use a lifestyle photo.

### **Mobile**

Keep the eyebrow, headline, description and primary CTA inside the first viewport. Place the dashboard preview immediately below. The secondary link anchors to the sample analysis.

## **Fold 2 \- Enterprise engagement and outcome proof**

### **Objective**

Establish credibility while keeping logo status and outcome attribution accurate.

### **Final copy**

Headline: Engagement with leaders across sectors  
Description: Across CPG and durables, automotive, real estate, retail and media, public sector and more.  
Supporting line: Plus a growing clientele of 25+ SMBs.

Logo specification  
Use all 27 organization logos below, with no substitutions. Approved source: slide 9 of the latest Introduction to NeoCore presentation: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aUsf-3kz0klRNna2g7VCVtzAYRlyEsmv/view

Exact logo set  
• CPG / Durables: Diageo, P\&G, ITC Limited, Eureka Forbes, Panasonic, Mamaearth and Page Industries Limited  
• Automotive: Ather, Mahindra Rise, Honda  
• Real Estate: Shriram Properties, HomeLane  
• Retail / Media: The Souled Store, Sony Entertainment Television, Specsmakers, BIG FM and Zee Entertainment Enterprises (“Z” mark; use the exact slide 9 artwork)  
• Public Sector: Government of Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh Police  
• Others: Bodycraft, Emirates, Larsen & Toubro (L\&T), Matrix Life Science, ACKO, OM Logistics Supply Chain, Hindustan Petroleum (HP) and CHRIST (Deemed to be University)

Pilot-status treatment

Use a compact two-row logo wall on desktop. Keep logos optically balanced and monochrome only if brand rules allow. On mobile, use a manually scrollable logo strip; do not use an auto-playing carousel.

### **Outcome band**

70%+ \- Utilization reported for the always-on option  
\+15% \- Increase in lines per store in a leading FMCG rollout  
\+20% \- Increase in sales per store in the same rollout

### **Footnote**

Deployment outcomes are contextual and are not attributable to every organization shown.

### **Claim rule**

Use only the three proof figures above, with the stated context and footnote.

## **Fold 3 \- How NeoCore works**

### **Objective**

Bridge from the familiar CRM limitation to one simple, repeatable explanation of the product mechanism.

### **Final copy**

Problem bridge: Your CRM shows what happened. Frontline conversations reveal why.  
Supporting line: Manual notes and occasional ride-alongs leave most field conversations invisible. NeoCore turns them into structured intelligence managers can act on.  
Section headline: Turn conversations into management intelligence.

### **Five-step flow**

1\. Capture  
Neo One captures frontline conversations with minimal added effort.

2\. Understand  
NeoCore processes speech in 100+ languages, separates speakers and understands company-specific vocabulary.

3\. Structure  
Custom fields map each conversation against the messages, questions and steps the sales motion requires.

4\. Aggregate  
Signals roll up across representatives, teams, regions, products and time in one management view.

5\. Act  
Leaders see adherence gaps, coaching priorities and Voice of Customer themes while they are still actionable.

### **Representation**

Build one continuous annotated platform flow:  
Neo One capture → NeoCore processing → Custom fields → Centralized dashboard → Management action

Place steps 2–5 inside one large container labelled “NeoCore intelligence layer.” That container must occupy at least 80% of the composition. Use NeoCore’s real dashboard or representative UI to show team-, region- and time-level aggregation. Do not represent all five stages as equal-sized feature cards.

### **Motion**

A restrained scroll-triggered reveal may move one conversation signal through the flow. Respect reduced-motion settings and ensure the complete meaning remains visible without animation.

## **Fold 4 \- Management outcomes and enterprise capabilities**

### **Objective**

Make the output tangible and show how management turns visibility into better execution.

### **Final copy**

Headline: Turn visibility into better frontline execution.  
Description: NeoCore makes conversations queryable and comparable, giving leaders the evidence to improve how teams sell and learn.

### **Primary outcome cards**

1\. Measure pitch adherence  
Define the messages, questions and steps that matter. NeoCore structures each conversation against those custom fields and shows where execution is consistent or slipping.

2\. Coach with evidence  
Identify repeated behaviours and missed steps, then focus coaching on the representatives, teams and regions that need it most.

3\. Hear the Voice of Customer  
Aggregate objections, competitor mentions, product feedback and emerging market themes while they are still actionable.

Preserve this visual and narrative order: adherence first, coaching second, Voice of Customer third. Give the first two cards slightly more visual weight than the third.

### **Enterprise capability rail**

Breakthrough technology  
Multilingual processing, speaker attribution, emotion capture and processing in under two minutes.

Tailored to your needs  
Tune NeoCore for local brands, products, competitors, industry terminology and regional sales language.

Built for adoption  
Friction-light capture minimizes additional administrative work for frontline teams.

API-first  
Connect NeoCore intelligence with CRM, BI and enterprise workflows through APIs and MCP.

### **Ungated sample-analysis module**

Headline: See what NeoCore produces.  
Show the following complete synthetic example without requesting visitor information.

### **Conversation signal**

“Brand X offers us a better margin. I can stock this product if your scheme improves.”

### **Structured intelligence**

• Pitch adherence: 4 of 5 required points covered  
• Missed topic: Current retailer scheme  
• Coaching priority: Address the margin objection using the approved comparison  
• Voice of Customer: Competitor margin pressure  
• Next action: Follow up with the updated scheme

Label: Illustrative synthetic example

### **Representation**

On desktop, show Conversation signal → Structured fields → Management action as three connected panels. Stack them in the same order on mobile. The sample must be fully readable, not blurred or partially gated.

### **CTA below sample**

See a tailored demo  
Use an outline treatment. It opens the qualification form and remains visually subordinate to “Talk to our enterprise team.”

## **Fold 5 \- Enterprise data, security and integrations**

### **Objective**

Give IT, security and procurement stakeholders enough evidence to continue evaluation.

### **Final copy**

Headline: Enterprise-ready by design.  
Description: NeoCore combines configurable intelligence with the security, data controls and integrations required for enterprise deployment.

### **Data-flow visual**

Capture → Encrypted transfer → Process and structure → Redact configured PII → Deliver role-based intelligence and integrations

### **Proof ribbon**

• ISO 27001 certified  
• No audio storage by default  
• No training on customer data  
• India-resident servers  
• Configurable PII redaction  
• Role-based access  
• APIs and MCP

### **Representation**

Use a clean left-to-right data flow with an ISO 27001 badge and short proof labels. Do not use a generic shield illustration as the main visual. Use only official certification artwork supplied by NeoSapien.

### **Claim rule**

Use only the official ISO 27001 badge. Retain the exact wording “No audio storage by default.”

## **Fold 6 \- FAQ**

### **Objective**

Resolve the most common product, deployment and integration questions without interrupting the main narrative.

### **Representation**

Use a collapsed accordion. Open only the first item by default. Keep answers to two or three short sentences.

What is the difference between Neo One and NeoCore?  
Neo One captures frontline conversations. NeoCore processes, structures and aggregates those conversations into management intelligence for adherence, coaching and Voice of Customer.

Can NeoCore work across languages and company-specific terminology?  
Yes. NeoCore supports 100+ languages and can be tuned for product names, local brands, competitors, regional terminology and industry-specific language.

Can we define our own adherence criteria?  
Yes. Teams can configure the pitch points, questions, processes and follow-ups that matter to their sales motion. NeoCore structures captured conversations against those custom fields.

How does NeoCore improve coaching?  
It surfaces repeated behaviours, missed steps and execution gaps across representatives and teams, helping managers focus coaching on specific evidence rather than occasional observation.

Can NeoCore integrate with our existing systems?  
Yes. APIs and MCP can connect NeoCore with CRM, BI and other enterprise workflows. The precise integration scope is agreed during the pilot.

How is enterprise data handled?  
NeoCore is ISO 27001 certified, does not store audio by default, does not train models on customer data and uses India-resident servers. PII redaction and role-based access can be configured for the deployment.

What does an enterprise pilot include?  
A pilot defines the team, use case and success measures; configures company terminology and custom fields; deploys capture; measures results; and produces a rollout recommendation.

## **Fold 7 \- Enterprise pilot and final CTA**

### **Objective**

Turn interest into a clearly bounded next step.

### **Final copy**

Headline: Start with a focused enterprise pilot.  
Description: Choose one team, define the conversations and outcomes that matter, and validate NeoCore against your field reality.

Five-step pilot  
1\. Align  
Select the team, region, use case and success measures.

2\. Configure  
Add products, brands, competitors, terminology and adherence fields.

3\. Deploy  
Set up Neo One capture, NeoCore access and required integrations.

4\. Measure  
Track utilization, pitch adherence, coaching priorities and Voice of Customer themes.

5\. Review  
Assess results, integration requirements and the broader rollout plan.

Primary CTA  
Talk to our enterprise team

Supporting line  
We will scope the team, workflows, languages, integrations and success measures with you.

### **Representation**

Show the five steps as a compact horizontal sequence on desktop and a vertical timeline on mobile. End with a high-contrast CTA panel. Do not create a separate pilot fold elsewhere.

# **3\. Form and Calendly flow**

All primary CTAs and the tailored-demo CTA open the same short qualification form. Preserve the originating CTA and page section as hidden analytics fields.

### **Form heading**

Tell us about your frontline team.

### **Fields**

• Name \- required  
• Organization \- required  
• Official work email \- required; helper text: “Please use your organization email.”  
• Phone number \- required  
• Approximate device requirement \- optional dropdown:  
  • Not sure yet  
  • 1–49  
  • 50–99  
  • 100–249  
  • 250+

### **Submission flow**

1\. Save the lead to the agreed CRM or form endpoint.  
2\. Show a clear successful-submission state.  
3\. Redirect in the same tab to the 30-minute Enterprise Calendly page:  
[https://calendly.com/enterprise-neosapien/30min](https://calendly.com/enterprise-neosapien/30min)  
4\. Retain the lead even if the visitor does not complete the Calendly booking.  
5\. If lead capture fails, show an actionable error and do not redirect until the submission succeeds.  
6\. Preserve campaign, referrer and CTA-source parameters where available.

### **Form behavior**

Use inline validation, clear error text and accessible labels. Do not automatically reject every public-domain address; prompt for a work email and allow a manual path if needed.

# **4\. Responsive, accessibility and performance requirements**

• Desktop content width: approximately 1200–1280 px with generous side margins.  
• Hero proposition and primary CTA must be visible in the first mobile viewport.  
• Stack flows, cards and sample-analysis panels in their intended reading order.  
• Do not hide essential information in hover states.  
• Avoid auto-playing carousels, autoplay audio and heavy background video.  
• Respect reduced-motion preferences.  
• Meet WCAG AA color contrast and keyboard-navigation requirements.  
• Add descriptive alternative text for product visuals and meaningful logo labels.  
• Use responsive WebP or AVIF images and lazy-load below-fold media.  
• Target Largest Contentful Paint below 2.5 seconds on a typical mobile connection.  
• Reserve image dimensions to avoid layout shift.

# **5\. Analytics requirements**

### **Track**

• Navigation CTA click  
• Hero CTA click  
• Sample-analysis view  
• Tailored-demo CTA click  
• Form start  
• Form validation failure  
• Form submission  
• Calendly redirect  
• Calendly booking completion, where integration permits  
• FAQ expansion by question

### **Primary success measure**

Qualified Calendly bookings

### **Supporting measures**

Qualified form submissions, form completion rate, Calendly completion rate and sample-analysis engagement

# Neo Core — Landing Page Brief

# **NeoCore Enterprise Landing-Page Brief**

## *A concise brief for a focused enterprise conversion page*

Page scope: Large enterprises with distributed field or retail sales teams. The page leads with management visibility into field conversations, then shows how that visibility improves pitch and process adherence, enables targeted coaching and surfaces Voice of Customer signals.

# **1\. Objective**

Build a focused enterprise page that converts qualified buyers into conversations with NeoSapien’s enterprise team. Move quickly from the management-visibility promise to the solution: show how Neo One and NeoCore create centralized intelligence, how leaders use it for adherence, coaching and Voice of Customer, how access is governed and what the next step involves.

**Primary conversion: A qualified request to speak with NeoSapien’s enterprise team.**

# **2\. Positioning**

Category: Frontline conversation intelligence for enterprise sales.

Core promise: Give management visibility into approved field-sales conversations—with minimal added effort for representatives.

Broad positioning: NeoCore is the enterprise intelligence layer for field-sales conversations that existing systems capture inconsistently. Neo One captures approved conversations with minimal added rep effort; NeoCore processes, structures and centralizes them so management can measure pitch and SOP adherence, coach teams and hear the Voice of Customer at scale.

Messaging pillars: Minimal-effort capture and high adoption; centralized management visibility; adherence through configurable fields; targeted coaching; multilingual processing tuned to company vocabulary; role-based access and PII redaction; integrations and governed deployment.

# **3\. Audience and buying group**

1. Primary buyer — Sales Excellence / Revenue Transformation / GTM Excellence leader. Owns field effectiveness and the pilot business case; needs visibility across teams and regions, configurable adherence measures, targeted coaching priorities and a scalable operating model.  
2. Technical gatekeeper — CIO / IT / Information Security. Evaluates consent, data flow, security, retention, role-based access, redaction, accuracy, integrations and deployment governance.  
3. Executive sponsor — CRO / business head / CXO. Wants evidence that the platform can improve sales execution, customer understanding and management decision-making at scale.  
4. Operational champion — Regional sales leader / sales enablement / L\&D. Converts the intelligence into coaching, playbooks, SOP improvement and field action.  
5. End user — Field or retail sales representative. Needs transparent, approved capture with minimal added effort and no post-conversation logging burden.  
6. Initial enterprise profile — Large organizations with distributed field or retail sales teams. Lead with FMCG, consumer durables and automotive.  
7. Page focus — Sales conversation intelligence for enterprise deployments. Other segments, partner journeys and direct device purchase belong on separate pages.

Page rule: The business buyer owns the hero and pilot case; IT and security receive the proof required to approve deployment. Governance should support the sale without taking over the opening narrative.

# **4\. Recommended hero**

Headline options — Option 1 is recommended.

**Option 1 — Make frontline sales conversations visible, measurable and actionable.**

Option 2 — Turn field sales conversations into actionable intelligence.

Option 3 — Turn field sales conversations into intelligence that improves adherence and coaching.

Option 4 — Your CRM shows what happened. Field conversations reveal why.

Why Option 1 is strongest: It identifies the source of intelligence and ties it directly to the two highest-priority enterprise outcomes. The remaining options are useful testing directions.

Description: Neo One captures approved conversations with minimal added effort. NeoCore turns them into centralized intelligence so leaders can measure pitch and SOP adherence, coach teams and hear the Voice of Customer—across regions and languages.

Primary CTA: Talk to our enterprise team. Clicking the CTA opens a short qualification form; after submission, the visitor is redirected to the [30-minute Enterprise Calendly](https://calendly.com/enterprise-neosapien/30min).

Hero image: A clear visibility composition: an authentic field customer conversation enters through Neo One as a discreet capture input; NeoCore processes and structures it into configurable fields; a central management dashboard shows adherence, coaching opportunities and Voice of Customer signals. The platform and management view must dominate. Avoid an isolated device beauty shot, generic AI art, stock boardrooms or any covert-recording cue.

Proof line beneath CTA: Prioritize approved adoption evidence—such as verified utilization or conversation-capture rate—followed by supported language coverage, processing latency, security credentials or deployment scale. If facts are not approved, omit the line rather than use placeholders.

# **5\. Fold-by-fold page plan**

## Fold 1 — Hero: Category, outcome and action

Objective: Establish the solution category, management outcome and primary action in seconds.

Content: Recommended headline and description, one dominant “Talk to our enterprise team” CTA that opens the short qualification form, the subordinate security link and one approved proof line.

Representation: A high-level visibility composition: approved conversation → NeoCore intelligence → central management view. Make adherence the first visible output, followed by coaching and Voice of Customer; show the promise rather than process detail, and let the solution fold below provide product depth.

## Fold 2 — Trust: Make the offer credible

Objective: Reduce immediate skepticism and make NeoCore safe to share internally.

Content: Use the approved customer and partner logos as a trust strip. Directly below it, show three cross-customer benefit signals supplied by the sales team: 70%+ utilization, 2× adherence and 20%+ increase in sales per FTE. Present them as aggregate NeoCore outcomes, not as claims attributed to any individual logo.

Representation: One thin approved-logo strip followed by a separate three-metric benefit line: “70%+ utilization” | “2× adherence” | “20%+ sales per FTE”. Keep the two rows visually distinct and verify the final claim wording and source before publication.

## Fold 3 — How NeoCore turns conversations into management action

Objective: Move directly into the solution and show how centralized visibility becomes adherence, coaching and Voice of Customer action—without repeating the hero.

Content: Neo One captures approved conversations with minimal added effort and should appear only as the small capture input. NeoCore is the intelligence layer: it performs multilingual synthesis, recognizes organization-specific vocabulary, structures each conversation into configurable fields, aggregates signals across teams and regions and turns them into centralized management insights. Show the use priority explicitly: adherence first, coaching second and Voice of Customer third, using frontline examples from FMCG, consumer durables or automotive.

Representation: Use the latest deck’s “Our solution \- NeoCore” slide as the structural reference, but rebalance it for the website: Neo One and capture should occupy no more than 20% of the visual hierarchy; NeoCore, its dashboard and its intelligence outputs should occupy at least 80%. Show a small frontline conversation and Neo One input feeding a dominant NeoCore layer for synthesis, organization-specific structuring and enterprise aggregation, then the management outputs—adherence, coaching and Voice of Customer. Carry security and access control across the data flow rather than as a disconnected badge.

## Fold 4 — Why NeoCore works at enterprise scale

Objective: Explain the four product strengths that make NeoCore usable and valuable in real enterprise deployments.

Content: Four sections—Breakthrough technology: multilingual synthesis, speaker attribution, low latency and emotion capture, using only validated figures and claims. Tailored to your needs: organization-specific context, lingo, vocabulary and configurable outputs. Easy usage for real business outcomes: minimal-effort capture designed for high utilization and measurable operational impact, with public metrics only after validation. API-first: structured signals integrate into the organization’s CRM, SFA, LMS, BI or internal systems.

Representation: Present the four sections as one clean capability rail or two-by-two layout, each anchored by product proof or representative UI—not generic icons. Below it, show a useful synthetic sample analysis before offering “Explore a tailored demo” as a subordinate secondary CTA. Gate only the full analysis or tailored demo behind minimal business details; keep “Talk to our enterprise team” visually primary.

## Fold 5 — Enterprise intelligence and integration

Objective: Show NeoCore as an organizational intelligence layer, not a collection of individual recordings.

Content: Aggregate by team, region, store, language, topic and configured field; connect approved structured signals to CRM, SFA, LMS or internal systems; distinguish standard product capabilities from custom services.

Representation: Architecture diagram from approved capture to NeoCore to client systems, paired with a regional or topic dashboard view.

## Fold 6 — Security, privacy and consent

Objective: Show that the organization can control both who sees conversation-derived intelligence and what sensitive information is visible.

Content: Show the governed data flow from approved capture through processing and management access: role-based permissions; scoped access by team, region or use case; PII and sensitive-information redaction; consent and recording controls; encryption in transit and at rest; retention, deletion, data residency and auditability—using approved current facts only. Clarify what is redacted, whether redaction is automatic or configurable and when it occurs.

Representation: One annotated security data-flow diagram across capture → processing → redaction → encrypted storage → permissioned access, paired with a small role-access matrix and redacted-transcript example. Add a compact certification ribbon showing ISO 27001 only. Do not show SOC 2 or HIPAA until achieved and approved for publication; keep “Review security & accuracy” as a subordinate link.

## Fold 7 — FAQ: Resolve evaluation questions

Objective: Resolve the questions that otherwise surface late in evaluation.

Content: Accuracy, languages, noisy conditions, consent, connectivity, retention, data access, integrations, implementation, pricing approach and support.

Representation: Short, direct accordion answers with links to technical evidence. Move any essential differentiator into the main narrative.

## Fold 8 — Final CTA and bounded enterprise pilot

Objective: Convert accumulated confidence into one clear, low-risk next step.

Content: Restate the outcome, repeat “Talk to our enterprise team” and explain the two-step path: complete the short qualification form, then choose a 30-minute slot on the Enterprise Calendly. After the conversation, frame the pilot in five steps: 1\) choose one frontline workflow and pilot cohort; 2\) confirm geography, language scope and required devices; 3\) agree the baseline, success metrics and governance checkpoints; 4\) deploy and review evidence; and 5\) make a scale decision.

Representation: Use a short single-column form with exactly five visible fields: Name; Organization; Total number of devices required; Official email ID (prompt: “Please use your official work email”); and Phone number. On submission, redirect to the [30-minute Enterprise Calendly](https://calendly.com/enterprise-neosapien/30min). State clearly what happens next. Place a compact five-step pilot blueprint beside or immediately below the form, keeping timing, device count and commercial terms flexible until standardized. After a useful synthetic preview, offer “Explore a tailored demo” only as a subordinate secondary CTA.

# **6\. Page-wide direction**

* Tone: Calm, precise and enterprise-credible. Use customer language and outcome verbs. Avoid inflated AI claims and language that suggests employee monitoring.  
* Visual system: Real field context, real or representative product UI and simple diagrams. The central management view, custom-field adherence and coaching decisions should dominate; the wearable should appear only where the capture mechanism needs explanation.  
* Navigation: How it works, Outcomes, Accuracy & security, FAQs and Pilot & next step, plus one persistent enterprise-team CTA. On mobile, preserve the headline, proof and CTA before optional imagery.  
* Conversion: Use “Talk to our enterprise team” as the only dominant CTA. After a useful synthetic preview, offer “Explore a tailored demo” as a subordinate secondary CTA that gates only the full analysis or tailored demo behind minimal business details. “Review security & accuracy” remains a text link for the technical evaluation path.

# **7\. Required before publication**

* Approve the public product language and the explicit division of roles: Neo One captures approved conversations; NeoCore processes, structures and centralizes the intelligence.  
* Confirm current encryption, hosting, data-residency, role-based access and scoped-permission claims. Show ISO 27001 only after current certification evidence is approved; keep SOC 2 and HIPAA off the public ribbon until achieved and approved.  
* Confirm the supported scope of configurable fields and organization-specific vocabulary, and separate standard capabilities and integrations from roadmap items or custom services.  
* Secure permission and evidence for every customer logo, utilization figure, latency or accuracy claim, deployment detail and quantified business result.  
* Standardize the five-step enterprise pilot scope, success criteria, governance checkpoints, commercial framing and support commitment before fixing timing, device count or terms publicly.

# **8\. Measurement**

* Primary KPI: Qualified requests to speak with the enterprise team.  
* Sales-quality KPIs: Target-account fit, buyer seniority, defined frontline use case, identified pilot team or region, meeting show rate, pilots started and pipeline created.

# Best Practices — B2B Landing Pages

# **B2B Landing-Page Best Practices**

## *One-page design guide*

A strong B2B page helps a skeptical buying group answer five questions quickly: Is this for me? What outcome will it create? How does it work? Can I trust it? What should I do next?

1. **Make the first screen explicit.** State the offer or category, priority audience, business outcome and distinctive mechanism in plain language. Pair it with one primary CTA, and mirror the promise made in the ad, email or referral source. [\[Google Ads\]](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6238826/optimising-your-ad-and-landing-page?hl=en-GB)  
2. **Design for a buying group, not a single lead.** Let the hero unify the commercial outcome; use lower sections to give the business sponsor, end user, IT/security, procurement and finance the evidence they need to approve and defend the choice. Forrester reports that the typical 2026 buying decision includes 13 internal stakeholders and nine external influencers. [\[Forrester\]](https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/)  
3. **Build one persuasive sequence.** Move from relevance → costly problem → believable mechanism → outcomes → proof → differentiation → risk reduction → objection handling → CTA. The exact fold count can vary; the buyer-question order should not.  
4. **Write for scanning.** Front-load important information, start headings with meaningful words, use short paragraphs and bullets, and remove jargon. NN/g’s eye-tracking work shows that weakly formatted pages invite shallow scanning; Unbounce’s large observational SaaS dataset also associates simpler copy with higher conversion. [\[NN/g — Scanning\]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/f-shaped-pattern-reading-web-content/) [\[Unbounce SaaS\]](https://unbounce.com/conversion-benchmark-report/saas-conversion-rate/)  
5. **Show the mechanism, not decoration.** Use the real product, workflow, UI, output or before/after operating model. Avoid generic executives, handshakes and abstract AI graphics: users scrutinize information-carrying images and often ignore decorative imagery. [\[NN/g — Imagery\]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/photos-as-web-content/)  
6. **Place proof beside the claim it validates.** Prefer approved customer logos, named quotes, quantified outcomes with timeframes, sample outputs, implementation facts and current security evidence. Professional design, clear company identity and restrained claims reinforce credibility. [\[Stanford Credibility\]](https://credibility.stanford.edu/guidelines/index.html)  
7. **Keep one dominant conversion path.** Repeat the same primary CTA after proof and objection-handling sections. Ask only for information needed to route or qualify the request, use a short single-column form, and explain what happens after submission. [\[W3C Forms\]](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/)  
8. **Design mobile-first, fast and accessible.** In Unbounce’s SaaS sample, mobile generated 79% of visits. Target LCP ≤2.5s, INP \<200ms and CLS \<0.1; meet WCAG 2.2 AA for contrast, keyboard access, labels and control sizing. [\[Unbounce SaaS\]](https://unbounce.com/conversion-benchmark-report/saas-conversion-rate/) [\[Google Core Web Vitals\]](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/core-web-vitals) [\[WCAG 2.2\]](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)  
9. **Measure business quality, not form volume.** Track qualified demo bookings, meeting show rate, pilot starts and pipeline by persona/source. Test one clear hypothesis at a time—headline, hero proof, CTA, form or case study—so the result is interpretable.

# B2B customer personas

**NeoSapien**

B2B Customer Segments and archetypes

# **Context**

4 segments for NeoSapien’s B2B sales (1) SMBs (2) Enterprises, (3) Bulk buyers/ resellers, (4) Government / public sector. 

SMBs contribute majority of current sales (50%+) in May and June; enterprises have started pilots across FMCG, Consumer durables, Real Estate and Auto. Sales to bulk/ resellers and government customers is nascent.

# **Segment 1: SMBs**

## **Archetype 1A — The Promoter (owner-champion)**

| Buyer profile | Promoter / founder / CEO of an SMB. Personally curious about AI tools; often the most tech-forward person in their own business. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **First interaction with NeoSapien** | Instagram and social content; word of mouth from colleagues or family members who own or have seen a Neo 1\. In multiple observed cases, they have already bought and used a Neo 1 personally before reaching out. |
| **Trigger for purchase** | A personal 'this works for me' moment translated into 'this could work for my team', reinforced by the novelty of the device — a first-of-its-kind AI wearable they want their business to adopt early. Verbatim: *“I have been using the product for the last month, and it is really helpful... I now want to roll it out to my team...”* |
| **KPCs** | **1\. Ease of use, language coverage –** Always-on, coverage of 100+ languages **2\. Near-term ROI** \- visible productivity or follow-up gains within weeks, not quarters **3\. Price** – Not interested in a high price subscription, anchors to website price and negotiates from there |
| **Purchase process** | Single decision maker; personal product experience substitutes for a formal POC. Timeline of **1–3 weeks from first connect** to order. Team-level rollout \[*typically 10–50 devices*\]. |
| **Typical use-case** | Personal assistant for the executive team; sales team copilot. |

## **Archetype 1B — Upper management (internal sponsor)**

| Buyer profile | Senior manager or functional head in an SMB. Not the final decision maker — the promoter / CEO is. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **First interaction with NeoSapien** | Same discovery channels as 1A: Instagram, colleagues, family. |
| **Trigger for purchase** | They want to bring the device into the business but must convince the promoter / CEO for a broader rollout — often by putting the device directly in the promoter's hands. Verbatim: *“I want to buy a device for my CEO/COO so that they can see for themselves what this can do.”* |
| **KPCs** | **Price** \- a pilot cheap enough to approve without too many questions from the promoter; low absolute spend matters more than unit economics **Proof points of efficacy** – Want to see sample notes, ask for complimentary demo units, in-person demos if possible |
| **Purchase process** | Buyer and decision maker are different people — this archetype is a champion, not the economic buyer. Timeline of **1–3 weeks from first connect**; order size of **1–5 devices**, sized to sit under internal approval thresholds. Expansion conversation follows once the promoter is convinced (archetype 1A dynamics). |
| **Typical use-case** | Personal assistant for the executive team (starting with the promoter / CEO / COO); sales team copilot on expansion. |

Integrations** into their existing apps / workflows **4\. Data privacy and security** \- incl. DPDPA compliance, SOC 2, ISO 27001 and VAPT **5\. Ease of use** \- to enable change management at scale |

Pilot closure can take from 3 weeks-3 months; pilot runs for 3-4 weeks post which scale order negotiation starts (This is a multi-month process) |

# Enterprise FAQ

*The answers below preserve the source document’s scope and caveats. Items marked “In progress” require current validation before use. The source PDF lists enterprise@neosapien.xyz; confirm the current enterprise inbox before publishing an email address.*

## 1\. Data Security and Privacy

**1\. Is NeoCore compliant with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA)?**  
NeoSapien is ISO 27001 certified; every third-party service in the platform stack meets SOC 2 compliance standards; and customer data is held on India-resident servers. In progress: full DPDPA compliance is expected within six to eight weeks. For personal-data deployments, NeoSapien acts as Data Processor for the customer, which is the Data Fiduciary, and a DPA is executed alongside the master service agreement before production data flows.  
**2\. Where is conversation and transcript data stored?**  
On India-resident production servers, supporting India-residency requirements in healthcare, financial services, government and similar deployments.  
**3\. Is raw audio retained on NeoSapien servers?**  
No, not by default. Raw audio is processed transiently and discarded after the transcript and structured outputs are generated. Short-term retention for audit or quality review can be separately agreed.  
**4\. What is the data retention policy for transcripts?**  
Transcripts are retained indefinitely unless deletion is requested. A defined window—such as 90 days, one year or seven years—can be agreed in the master service agreement and implemented through tenant lifecycle policies.  
**5\. Is customer data used to train NeoSapien’s models?**  
No. Conversation data is not used for model training or product improvement.  
**6\. How are personally identifiable information and personal conversations handled?**  
PII and personal or non-work conversations are detected and redacted in the processing pipeline, reducing stored sensitive content and personal data sent to downstream customer systems.  
**7\. How is data encrypted and access controlled?**  
All API traffic uses TLS. The API uses JWT authentication with token rotation and scoped access. Credentials can be scoped by integration, environment and service principal, and customers can rotate tokens at any time.  
**8\. How often is the platform audited?**  
Independent vulnerability testing and penetration audits occur every six months. Audit summaries and platform sub-processors’ SOC 2 status are available to enterprise customers under NDA.  
**9\. Can a specific memory or all data for a user be deleted on request?**  
Yes. A memory-deletion endpoint supports granular rights-request deletion; enterprise administrative APIs support bulk deletion by user or tenant. Contract-termination deletion follows DPA timelines.  
**10\. How are data breaches handled?**  
NeoSapien notifies the customer without undue delay after a confirmed breach affecting customer data. The customer handles onward regulator and data-principal notifications; NeoSapien supplies supporting information and assistance. Specific timelines are defined in the DPA.

## 2\. Transcript Quality and Content

**11\. What is the latency from speech to a synthesised, retrievable memory?**  
Approximately two minutes at P50 and ten minutes at P99, covering transcription, diarization and synthesis. Latency-sensitive workflows should design around P99. Sub-minute latency is on the roadmap and should not be assumed today.  
**12\. Does the memory object include the full raw transcript?**  
Yes.  
**13\. How accurate is speaker diarization in multi-speaker conversations?**  
The source states 87%+ for multi-agent conversations with clear audio. Significant ambient noise reduces accuracy by approximately four percentage points, so noisy deployments should be pilot-tested.  
**14\. What languages does the platform support?**  
More than 100 languages, with significant Indic-language coverage. Within-conversation code-switching, such as English and Hindi, is supported.  
**15\. How does the platform handle domain-specific vocabulary such as drug names, SKUs and brand names?**  
NeoCore has not been benchmarked on domain-specific lexicons and promises no incremental accuracy over its standard baseline. Customer-provided drug lists, SKUs, brand names and competitor names can be keyword-boosted; uplift varies and should be validated in a pilot.  
**16\. Is there a minimum audio duration for a memory to be created?**  
Yes. Very short utterances are filtered to suppress incidental sounds and false triggers. Customers needing single-word commands or brief acknowledgements should validate that they meet the threshold.  
**17\. Are the AI outputs suitable for clinical or regulated decision-making?**  
No. Transcripts, summaries and synthesised outputs are supplied “as is,” are not medical-grade, and do not replace human review in clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic or other regulated workflows. Customers must validate outputs before safety- or regulation-sensitive use.

## 3\. API Access

**18\. Is there a developer or enterprise API tier?**  
Yes. The documented NeoCore developer API is live and integrates with CRM, BI and analytics systems. Enterprise engagements include a stable API contract, sized rate limits and a named technical contact.  
**19\. What authentication does the API use?**  
JWT tokens with configurable lifetime. On expiry, the API returns an error; the integration should request a new token and retry using the standard JWT refresh pattern. No separate manual renewal is required.  
**20\. What rate limits apply?**  
Defaults support routine polling and typical multi-site volumes, including dozens of simultaneous sessions. Customers should provide expected call patterns during onboarding; exact limits and burst allowances are documented per tenant.  
**21\. Is a sandbox environment with mock data available?**  
No. Development uses the production API with a Neo 1 linked to the customer organisation. Customers generate real test memories and may delete them before go-live; this exercises the same code paths as production.  
**22\. Is the OpenAPI specification available as a downloadable file?**  
The specification is supplied as an importable Postman collection. No formal OpenAPI JSON or YAML export is currently published; the source says the collection is sufficient for most client-generation and request/response-validation needs.  
**23\. Are webhooks or streaming delivery supported?**  
Webhooks can announce memory creation but do not push the memory payload. The customer must then fetch it via API. This reduces polling but does not eliminate the API call; true content push should be raised during integration design.  
**24\. What is the API versioning and deprecation policy?**  
No formal policy is published yet. In practice, customers receive two weeks to one month of advance notice plus a defined backward-compatibility window; enterprise customers receive direct notice. In progress: formal policy definition.

## 4\. Reliability and Support

**25\. What uptime commitment does NeoCore offer?**  
Observed uptime is greater than 99%. There is currently no public status page. Enterprise target uptime, measurement methodology and any service credits are defined in the master service agreement or SLA schedule. In progress: a public status page.  
**26\. What support channel is available?**  
Email, Slack and WhatsApp, with a named technical contact. Response times, severity SLAs, escalation paths and on-call coverage are sized to deployment scale and agreed commercially.  
**27\. How are scheduled maintenance and incidents communicated?**  
Through the customer’s named support channel. Material tenant-impacting incidents receive a post-incident report.  
**28\. What happens to memories if the API is briefly unavailable?**  
Synthesis continues if the device remains connected to the NeoSapien cloud. Memories created while the customer integration cannot reach the API remain retrievable through the sync endpoint after recovery. This differs from device-side disconnection.

## 5\. Device Filtering and Management

**29\. How are memories associated with a device or user?**  
With the wearer’s account or user email, not a device serial number. Customers should assign each device to a named user and use user ID as the memory-routing key.  
**30\. Can the memory sync endpoint be filtered to a specific device?**  
It filters by user ID, not device ID. Customers maintain the user → device → asset mapping; NeoCore returns the user ID for contextual resolution.  
**31\. Does each memory carry a device identifier?**  
No. It carries user ID.  
**32\. Is there a device management API?**  
No dedicated API. User-to-device assignment occurs in the admin console; customers maintain asset-to-user mappings externally. NeoSapien can support structured bulk-assignment onboarding.  
**33\. What happens to memories captured while a device is offline?**  
The device has no local buffer and requires connectivity. Nothing is captured during an offline window; connectivity-variable deployments should provide a stable mobile-data path.  
**34\. Can role-based access control be applied to who sees which users’ memories?**  
Yes. Administrator and analyst visibility can be scoped to an individual user, a group or the full organisation—for example, limiting a regional manager to users in that region.

## 6\. Hardware

**35\. What is the Neo 1, and what does it do?**  
NeoSapien’s always-on ambient-listening wearable. It captures nearby conversation and streams it to NeoCore for transcription, diarization and synthesis. It is paired one-to-one with a user account and cannot operate as a shared or unassigned asset.  
**36\. How does the device connect to the cloud?**  
Over mobile data, typically through a paired smartphone. No per-site customer network infrastructure or IT setup is required, supporting field, vehicle and multi-site deployments; continuous connectivity is required.  
**37\. Does the device buffer memories when offline?**  
No. Offline conversations are not captured. In progress: on-device offline buffering is on the roadmap.  
**38\. What is the battery life?**  
Rated for 17 hours of continuous use per charge; noisy or high-activity continuous capture reduces it. Detailed runtime figures are in the enterprise datasheet. Charging is via USB-C.  
**39\. What is the form factor?**  
A small pendant-style wearable worn around the neck. Dimensions, weight and mounting options are in the product datasheet.  
**40\. What is the microphone configuration and audio capture range?**  
A multi-microphone array tuned for the wearer and nearby conversation at a typical distance of three metres. Noisy settings should be pilot-tested; diarization accuracy is said to fall by about four percentage points there.  
**41\. Can device firmware be updated remotely?**  
Yes, over the air during regular cloud connectivity. Material changes are notified in advance through the support channel.  
**42\. What is the warranty on the device?**  
A limited 12-month warranty from delivery against material defects, subject to the master purchase agreement. It excludes misuse, unauthorised modification and damage outside intended operating conditions.  
**43\. How many devices does a typical deployment need?**  
One per active wearer. Shift deployments should size for maximum concurrent wearers rather than total headcount; devices may be handed between shifts after account reassignment in the admin console. A small spare pool is recommended.  
**44\. What is the lead time on device orders?**  
Quantities, pricing tiers and delivery lead times are agreed in the master purchase agreement. Small orders—typically 100 devices or fewer—are dispatched faster than large production orders; large-rollout timing is confirmed commercially.  
**45\. What happens if a device is lost or stolen?**  
NeoSapien support can remotely deactivate it, preventing further uploads and unbinding it from the user account. Customers should report loss or theft promptly.

# Next step

# Lead form and Calendly handoff

Purpose: Qualify enterprise demand with minimal friction, then let the visitor book a 30-minute enterprise conversation immediately.  
Entry point: Every primary “Talk to our enterprise team” CTA opens this form.

## Required visible fields

* Name  
* Organization  
* Total number of devices required  
* Official email ID  
* Phone number

## Field guidance

* Official email ID — Helper text: “Please use your official work email.” Prompt rather than hard-block public email domains unless Sales decides otherwise.  
* Total number of devices required — Use a numeric field; do not impose an unapproved minimum or maximum.  
* Phone number — Include a country-code selector.

## Interaction and handoff

* Keep the form single-column and display all five fields on one screen where practical.  
* Recommended form button: Continue to scheduling.  
* On successful submission, save and route the lead, then redirect to the [30-minute Enterprise Calendly](https://calendly.com/enterprise-neosapien/30min).  
* Prefill the Calendly name and email fields where the integration permits, so the visitor is not asked twice.  
* If the redirect fails, show the same scheduling link as a clear fallback.

## Implementation requirements

* All five visible fields are required.  
* Use inline validation without clearing completed fields.  
* Add concise consent and privacy copy for collecting business contact details and a phone number before launch.  
* Retain source, campaign and landing-page attribution as hidden fields; do not add them to the visible form.

# Fold 3 — Visualization Options

# Fold 3 — Visualization Options

Decision: Option 1 is recommended. It is closest to the latest deck’s “Our solution \- NeoCore” slide, while correcting the hierarchy so the capture device is clearly an input and NeoCore is clearly the product’s value.

# Source structure from the latest deck

* Seamless conversation capture and synthesis: wearable capture plus voice AI.  
* Enterprise-level aggregation: a central NeoCore dashboard that synthesizes conversations across the organization.  
* Custom insights: pitch-adherence tracking, Voice of Customer chatbot and personalized coaching manuals.  
* API and MCP integration into the organization’s systems.

*Commercial note: the deck currently labels custom insights as an add-on under a separate commercial construct. Confirm whether that distinction remains current before the website implies these outputs are included by default.*

# Non-negotiable visual hierarchy

* Neo One and the capture moment: no more than 20% of the visual hierarchy.  
* NeoCore, its intelligence processing, dashboard and outputs: at least 80% of the visual hierarchy.  
* Make synthesis, organization-specific structuring, enterprise aggregation and custom insights visible—not just implied.  
* Order the management outcomes as adherence first, coaching second and Voice of Customer third.  
* Show security, redaction and role-based access across the data flow rather than as an isolated badge.

## Option 1 — Capture → NeoCore intelligence → management action

**Recommended**

* Composition: a small frontline-conversation and Neo One input on the left feeds a large NeoCore intelligence canvas across the centre and right.  
* Inside NeoCore: show multilingual synthesis, company vocabulary, configurable fields and aggregation as one connected layer.  
* Management view: use representative product UI to show an adherence dashboard first, coaching priorities second and Voice of Customer trends third.  
* Security: run a thin protection layer across the entire flow—approved capture, PII redaction, scoped access and governed export.  
* Why it works: it explains the complete product in one glance while making the device visibly subordinate.  
* Mobile: stack the small capture input above the dominant NeoCore dashboard and outcomes; retain the 20:80 hierarchy.

[NeoCore Fold 3 - Option 1 - Intelligence Flow.png](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IjAVtUDqMiMJe_BzZAwN3zt79bDj5IwG/view)

## Option 2 — NeoCore management command centre

* Composition: make a large central NeoCore dashboard the hero; show Neo One only as a small incoming-signal tile.  
* Use dashboard callouts to reveal the layers behind the interface: synthesis, configurable fields, regional aggregation and permissions.  
* Place adherence, coaching and Voice of Customer as ordered management actions around the dashboard—not as three equal product modules.  
* Strength: strongest expression of software value and enterprise pricing.  
* Risk: the capture mechanism is less immediately obvious, so retain one clear wearer/device annotation.

[NeoCore Fold 3 - Option 2 - Command Centre.png](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1K5L4zGHhWdzw1SBNDTupTibeWmDHaNoA/view)

## Option 3 — Conversation transformed into structured intelligence

* Composition: begin with one representative frontline conversation, pass it through a dominant NeoCore transformation layer and end with an aggregated management view.  
* Show the transformation explicitly: raw dialogue → redacted transcript → company vocabulary and custom fields → cross-team aggregation → actions.  
* Keep Neo One as a small source badge beside the conversation rather than as a standalone product panel.  
* Strength: best for explaining custom fields, organization-specific lingo and how adherence is measured.  
* Risk: can become process-heavy; use one conversation example and one dashboard, not a dense pipeline.

[NeoCore Fold 3 - Option 3 - Structured Intelligence.png](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HTZi152Sfopqhjel1Ul_7QdVYnq7fa4Q/view)

# Recommendation

Proceed with Option 1\. It answers Sripriya’s product-clarity concern, remains faithful to the latest deck and gives NeoCore the strongest perceived value. Use Option 2 as the alternate if the available dashboard UI is strong enough to carry the fold; use Option 3 only when explaining configurable fields needs greater emphasis.

# Creative guardrails

* Do not use three equal-width columns; that makes hardware, aggregation and custom insights look equally valuable.  
* Do not lead with an isolated pendant beauty shot or a wearable-first headline.  
* Do not use generic AI clouds, glowing brains, stock boardrooms or surveillance cues.  
* Use authentic Neo One imagery and real or representative NeoCore UI.  
* Do not publish dashboard metrics, badges or security claims until validated and approved.
